title: Producer Jayanta Mukherjee, Husband of Moushumi Chatterjee, Dies in Mumbai
excerpt: The son of singer-composer Hemant Kumar died on 12 November at his Khar residence in his late 70s, FWICE confirmed, after more than five decades of marriage.
body:
• Film producer Jayanta Mukherjee, husband of veteran actor Moushumi Chatterjee and son of singer-composer Hemant Kumar, died on 12 November in Mumbai.
  • He was in his late 70s and died at his residence in Khar due to age-related issues, FWICE president BN Tiwari told PTI, according to Bollywood Hungama and BizzBuzz.
  • His production credits included Mazaaq (1975) and Do Ladke Dono Kadke (1979), and the television serial Talaash (1992).
  • He is survived by Moushumi Chatterjee, whom he married in 1972, and their younger daughter Megha; the family had not issued a detailed public statement in the reports read.

Jayanta Mukherjee, a film producer who was the husband of veteran actor Moushumi Chatterjee and the son of legendary singer-composer Hemant Kumar, died on 12 November in Mumbai. Bollywood Hungama, IWMBuzz and BizzBuzz all reported the death on 13 November, placing him at the centre of two of Indian cinema's best-known families: the Mukherjee musical lineage on his father's side, and Moushumi Chatterjee's long career in Hindi and Bengali cinema on his wife's side.

He was in his late 70s and had been unwell for some time, the reports said. BN Tiwari, president of the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE), confirmed the death. Speaking to PTI, Tiwari said he died at his residence in Khar due to age-related issues, according to Bollywood Hungama and BizzBuzz.

"He passed away last evening due to age-related issues at his residence in Khar."

— BN Tiwari, President, FWICE, to PTI

A producer who worked behind the camera

Jayanta Mukherjee, known as Babu to family and close friends, kept a relatively low profile despite his family background, IWMBuzz reported. Where his father built his reputation in front of the microphone and as a composer, Jayanta worked behind the scenes in film and television production.

Bollywood Hungama listed his production credits as Mazaaq (1975), Do Ladke Dono Kadke (1979) and Biwi Aur Makan (1966), noting that Mazaaq and Do Ladke Dono Kadke featured Moushumi Chatterjee in prominent roles, and that he was also associated with the television serial Talaash, which aired in 1992. IWMBuzz listed the same two 1970s Hindi films and Talaash, and BizzBuzz reported the same credits, adding that he worked in the music department of Biwi Aur Makan.

The family he came from

His father, Hemant Kumar — also known as Hemanta Mukherjee — was one of the most recognised singer-composers in Indian cinema, with work across Hindi and Bengali film music that continues to be widely heard. Bollywood Hungama described him as one of the most recognised singers and music composers in Indian cinema, and IWMBuzz said his contribution as a playback singer and composer remains cherished by music lovers.

That background placed Jayanta inside film music from birth, even though his own career took a production path rather than a singing or composing one. The reports read for this article do not credit him with carrying forward his father's performing career; they credit him as a producer and television producer in his own right.

Marriage and family

Jayanta Mukherjee and Moushumi Chatterjee married in 1972 and were together for more than five decades, all three sources reported. Moushumi Chatterjee became one of the most recognisable faces of Hindi and Bengali cinema in the 1970s and 1980s, IWMBuzz reported.

The couple had two daughters, Payal and Megha. Their elder daughter, Payal Mukherjee, died in December 2019 at the age of 45 following health complications, Bollywood Hungama and IWMBuzz reported. Jayanta is survived by Moushumi Chatterjee and their younger daughter Megha, both outlets reported. BizzBuzz reported that he is survived by his wife and two children; the more detailed reports in Bollywood Hungama and IWMBuzz name Megha as the surviving daughter, following Payal's death in 2019.

What has not been announced

The family had not shared a detailed public statement in the reports published on 13 November, Bollywood Hungama reported. IWMBuzz reported that details of the cause of death beyond the FWICE account and of the last rites had not yet been made available at the time of its report.

For diaspora readers who grew up with Hemant Kumar's songs and Moushumi Chatterjee's films in Bengali and Hindi, Jayanta Mukherjee's death closes a direct family link between those two bodies of work. Further reporting is available from IWMBuzz.
